subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI, what credential identity should own reusable-session auth epochs when both a local CLI credential and an OpenClaw auth profile exist but the local credential source presence changes?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix can either preserve continuity or weaken an auth/session boundary unless maintainers define how unproven Claude CLI identity should behave.

options.title: Narrow Identity-Stable Fix
options.body: Keep same-identity storage-source flips from rotating epochs, but preserve fail-closed resets when the host/profile identity changes or cannot be proven.

options.title: Approve Host-Only Contract
options.body: Make Claude CLI local host credentials the session auth owner and intentionally ignore cosmetic OpenClaw profile changes after security review.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Leave current invalidation semantics in place and document user-side mitigation for setups that share Claude CLI credentials across storage sources.

recommendation.title: Narrow Identity-Stable Fix
recommendation.body: Keep same-identity storage-source flips from rotating epochs, but preserve fail-closed resets when the host/profile identity changes or cannot be proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal on the CLI auth invalidation behavior and related session reset semantics.
